items.body:
## Observed

On 2026-11-06, queue-worker lanes repeatedly claimed tasks from `repo-health-code-pilot`, found `assigned_lane = opencode` on every one, checkpointed `handed_off`, and parked them for the opencode claimant — and no claimant session was ever launched. The lane-ledger rows keep `executed_lane = null` and `session_id = null` across every cycle.

Lane code-k shift 2026-11-06 15:13–15:30Z alone handed off five tasks this way:

- task 11066 (issue #6295, triage) — attempts 2/6; also handed off by earlier lanes today
- task 10832 (issue #6405, triage) — attempts 5/8, handed off repeatedly all day
- task 10950 (issue #6459, small_fix) — attempts 4/4 (at cap)
- task 11181 (issue #6282, triage) — attempts 1/6
- task 10751 (issue #4000, triage) — attempts 11/12, handed off repeatedly since 2026-11-05

The prior lane code-k shift (14:36Z handoff snapshot) recorded the same pattern for task 11174 (issue #6523): handed off twice (13:49Z and 14:35Z) with no launch in between. Its snapshot is at `hidden_files/lane-handoff-repo-health-code-pilot-k.json` in the goal workspace (overwritten each shift; the 15:30Z version carries this shift's five).

## Defect (suspected)

`opencode-claimant` polls every 10 minutes for claimed, opencode-assigned, unbound tasks and launches a session bound at launch time (worker instruction §1b). For these tasks the poll either never sees them (they sit `parked` with `work/assigned` between handoffs, and are only `claimed` for the brief handoff window), or sees them and fails to bind/launch without recording anything on the ledger row. Either way the cycle is claim → handed_off → park (20 min) → re-claim → handed_off, burning attempts (task 10751 is at 11/12, task 10950 at 4/4) with zero execution.

## Related, but distinct

- #5400 — `bind_repo_task_lane_session` guarded recovery mode dropped by migration-0023 (recovery rejects expired leases). Related: may block relaunch after a lease expires, but these tasks were never bound in the first place (`session_id` null from the start).
- #5508 — poll.py re-offers tasks whose `progress.session_id` was cleared while a ledger binding remains. Opposite shape: there a binding exists and should suppress re-offering; here no binding ever appears.

## Impact

- Every opencode-assigned task in the code pilot queue is effectively unworkable right now: workers can only hand off and park, per §1b they must not work or launch these tasks themselves.
- Attempt budgets drain on handoff cycles (task 10751 at 11/12, task 10950 at 4/4) — the same capped-at-max_attempts failure mode repaired on 2026-10-26 for tasks 1063/1111/1114/1115.

## Acceptance

- Root cause identified: claimant poll output/logs for one named task above (e.g. task 10751) show whether it was seen, skipped, or failed at bind/launch, and why.
- A handed-off task is launched by the claimant within one poll cycle of its handoff, or the handoff protocol is changed so workers stop cycling tasks the claimant cannot take (e.g. park with a claimant-visible state instead of a 20-minute timer).
- Attempt counting no longer charges a task for a handoff cycle in which no execution was attempted.

## Acceptance criteria
- Handed-off tasks (assigned_lane=opencode) are actually launched by the opencode claimant: the lane-ledger row for a handed-off task gains a non-null executed_lane and session_id, and the bound session posts its first checkpoint.
- A handed-off task that cannot be launched surfaces loudly (ledger row records the failure/reason, or the task is blocked with a named reason class) instead of silently cycling claim → handed_off → park → re-claim.
- Handoff cycles stop burning attempt budget for work never executed: a task handed off repeatedly with no launch does not advance toward max_attempts unclaimability (or the burn is explicitly surfaced in queue health).
- Regression evidence: at least one previously stuck handed-off task from the code pilot queue (e.g. task 10751 / issue #4000 or task 10950 / issue #6459) is observed launched end-to-end after the fix.

items.title: Conductor census helper session-count.py pages /api/session at limit=1000; the API caps limit at 200 — exit-3 census has stopped all conductor dispatch since 15:23Z
items.body:
## Symptom

`python3 /home/user/tools/session-count.py` — the mandated conductor capacity census — exits 3 with `session enumeration FAILED: HTTPError: HTTP Error 400: Bad Request` on every run since 2026-11-20T15:23Z. The runbook treats a census enumeration failure as a global stop, so the conductor's DISPATCH phase has been fully stopped for 6 consecutive cycles (15:23Z, 15:40Z, 16:00Z, 16:20Z, 16:40Z, and the in-flight cycle) while queued work exists in the pilot queues. The queue lanes themselves are still claiming; only conductor dispatch is gated.

## Evidence (2026-11-20, laptop-local)

- Live repro: `curl 'http://localhost:3000/api/session?limit=1000'` → HTTP 400 `{"_tag":"InvalidRequestError","message":"Expected a value less than or equal to 200\n  at [\"limit\"]","kind":"Query"}`. `limit=200` → HTTP 200 with cursor pagination; `limit=201` → 400. The helper sends `PAGE = 1000` (`list_sessions()` builds `/api/session?limit=1000`), so its very first page now fails.
- The helper worked at 14:41Z and 15:05Z (conductor-log.md: census succeeded, `unfinished roots 15/30` then `3/30`) and first failed at 15:23Z — the OpenChamber server side began enforcing the OpenCode ceiling in that window (exact restart/trigger not pinned; the enforcement itself is confirmed live above).
- The ceiling is already known and documented inside OpenChamber: commit `b003844b3` (2026-11-17, "fix(sessions): list sessions at most 200 a page, OpenCode's ceiling") added `SESSION_LIST_MAX_LIMIT = 200` with the comment *"OpenCode rejects a session.list `limit` above this with a 400 ('Expected a value less than or equal to 200'), which fails the whole list."* OpenChamber's own callers were fixed; the conductor helper was not.
- Impact record: conductor-log.md entries for the six stopped cycles (lines ~4111 onward), each recording the exact exit-3 failure and `sessions dispatched: 0`.
- A naive fix is incomplete: the helper already implements cursor pagination, but with `PAGE = 200` and the current `MAX_PAGES = 20` it would silently truncate at 4,000 of ~29,000 history rows; activity-map sessions older than that would surface as `unlisted N > 0`, which the mandate also treats as a stop condition.

## Root cause (verified, not suspected)

The helper violates the API contract: it pages `/api/session` with `limit=1000` while the endpoint (OpenChamber proxying OpenCode's session.list) validates `limit ≤ 200`. Everything else in the helper (cursor handling, activity-map population, counting rule) is unaffected.

## Ask

1. Fix `~/tools/session-count.py`: set `PAGE = 200` and raise `MAX_PAGES` enough to cover full history (~29k rows today → ≥150 pages; 400 gives headroom). The script is untracked local tooling under `~/tools`, so this needs Drew's word or a direct laptop edit — two constants, no logic change.
2. Until then the conductor stays in census-failure global stop, recording `sessions dispatched: 0` each cycle; the runbook is being followed, not bypassed.

Searched open and closed issues across the four repos (`session-count`, `session enumeration`, `conductor census`, `limit 200` in openchamber): no existing report. Related but different: #11764 (control-API 4s timeouts that stop the lane overlap checks — same family of laptop-tooling faults, different endpoint and failure).

Queue: deliberately not queued, same rationale as #11764: the deliverable is a file outside every repo (`~/tools/session-count.py`, untracked), and modifying Drew's mandated measurement instrument needs his sanction; a repo-pilot worker has no compliant worktree for it. Filed by the fleet conductor cycle (ses_e5e062bb3c8ffeNiJumoJZvan1) whose dispatch gate this failure has closed.

Parent: [#6018](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6018) (Atlas ingestion program). Statement S34 of the 2026-11-04 brief. **This is a task to execute, not only a design.**

## Task (Drew, in substance)

**Scan all existing embeds and determine whether they use the appropriate path or details.** The current corpus (107,639 chunks across the production monolith and the restored shards) accumulated over multiple ingestion eras with different conventions. The program's provenance standard (extensions on [#3125](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/3125)) requires every embed to carry a correct origin mark — `repo@hash:path` for git content, or a source-system mark (system @ machine @ date) for the rest. This audit measures how much of the existing corpus meets that bar and produces the defect list a repair pass would work from.

## Scope

- Inventory the provenance/path metadata actually present per chunk source class: well-formed `repo@hash:path`? path without hash? hash without path? free-text source strings? nothing?
- Correctness, not just presence: does the recorded path exist at the recorded hash? Do source-system marks name the right machine/date (e.g. session chunks attributed to the wrong host store)? Sampled verification against the live sources (repos on the laptop, the OpenCode DBs, the canonical atlas content stores: internal 18,235 sessions / 70,987 messages + secret 90 / 564 per the restoration records).
- Duplicates and orphans: chunks whose provenance points at sources that no longer exist, and duplicate chunks carrying divergent provenance (same content, different claimed origins) — both are logged states per the standard, and the audit counts them.
- Tier split throughout: report internal and secret tiers separately; handle secret-tier findings under the classification task's sensitivity rules (sibling task under [#6018](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6018) — counts and IDs, never content).

## Done looks like

A dated audit report: per-class counts (well-formed / defective-by-kind / missing), sampled-verification results, and a sized repair backlog (fixable by re-derivation from sources vs needs re-ingest vs unrecoverable-but-logged) filed as follow-ons. The audit itself changes no data.

items.body:
## Summary

The zero-message verification in `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py` (prompt.md step 1a, the #4758 / design #4912 recovery rule) calls an endpoint the v2 server does not have:

```
claimant.py:253  GET http://127.0.0.1:13420/api/session/<id>/messages
```

The live server serves the **singular** `/message` (returning `{"data": [...], "cursor": ...}`). `/messages` is a **404 with an empty body** — verified on `http://127.0.0.1:13420` on 2026-11-08:

```
GET /api/session/ses_e5e441ca753ffdMse0Sd5IZ977/message   -> 200  data[50], cursor
GET /api/session/ses_e5e441ca753ffdMse0Sd5IZ977/messages  -> 404  (empty body)
```

`poll.py` and the fire probe already use the singular form (`fire-probe.py` `session_messages()`); only `claimant.py` — and the stub in `test/test_claimant.py:75`, which pins the wrong path — use `/messages`.

## Why this is fail-open, not merely inert

The block at `claimant.py:250-265` is:

```python
messages_response = subprocess.run(["curl", "-s", "-m", "5",
    f"http://127.0.0.1:13420/api/session/{session_id}/messages"], ...)
if messages_response.returncode == 0:
    message_count = len(json.loads(messages_response.stdout or "[]"))
    if message_count == 0:
        recovery_candidates.append(...)
```

`curl -s` exits **0** on a 404, and the 404 body is empty, so:

1. `returncode == 0` → true,
2. `stdout or "[]"` → `"[]"` (the `or` was written for a timeout producing empty output),
3. `message_count == 0` → **every** stuck-bound row passes the zero-message gate.

The session GET immediately above it has the same shape (`claimant.py:217-231`): an unauthenticated `curl -s` returns a 401 `{"_tag": ...}` body, which is parsed and has no `id`, so the session is treated as **gone**. Chained together in live mode, the step-1 path is:

session GET → 401 body, no `id` → "gone" → attempts remain → messages read → 404 empty body → "0 messages" → recovery candidate → `DELETE` (401, `returncode == 0`, recorded as success — #7367) → `bind --launched-by opencode-claimant-recovery:zero-message-deleted` clears both bindings.

That is precisely the ordering the packet's step 1b forbids: an un-deleted session holding messages, with its binding cleared, leaving the task launchable for a second session while the first may still be alive. Today the only thing preventing it is that `supervision_step`'s candidate list comes from `repo-queue list` parsed as JSON, which fails (#7325), so the list is empty. The safety is incidental, not structural.

## Not covered by the open issues

- **#7367** (open) covers the missing Basic-auth header and "returncode is not a success test" for the delete. It does not cover the wrong path: with auth fixed, `/messages` still 404s and the empty-body `or "[]"` still reads as zero messages.
- **#7356** (open) covers `launch_step` never sending the prompt.
- **#4758** is closed against the rule's design, not against this implementation.

## Fix direction

1. One transport helper (per #7367) with a **path** constant, using `GET /api/session/<id>/message` and reading `data` from the envelope.
2. Treat an empty body, a non-2xx status, or a body that is not a message list as **unknown**, never as zero: the step-1a rule already says "if the message read is unavailable/incomplete, treat the state as unknown … leave it bound and stop". The current `stdout or "[]"` inverts that.
3. `test/test_claimant.py:75` must stub the singular path, and the fail-closed test should assert that a 404/empty messages read emits **no** `bind` argv and leaves the binding intact (it currently stubs an empty-body-free `"[]"`, so it cannot fail).

## Acceptance

- With the stub transport returning 404 + empty body for the messages read (and a live session object for the per-id GET), no recovery `bind` is emitted and no `DELETE` is issued.
- With the stub returning `{"data": [ ... 50 messages ... ]}`, no recovery candidate is produced.
- With the stub returning `{"data": []}` and every other stuck-bound fact true, the DELETE and atomic recovery `bind` are emitted, in that order.
- `grep -rn '/messages' pm-stack/opencode-claimant/` returns nothing outside the retired implementation docs (README.md:96, IMPLEMENTATION_CHECKLIST.md:206 also name the wrong path).

Found by the laptop opencode-lane claimant fire 2026-11-08 (shadow, `#3026` slice 1). Shadow report: `~/.local/state/opencode-claimant/shadow-fire-20261108T161653Z.json`.

## Acceptance criteria

- The zero-message gate in `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py` queries the endpoint the v2 server actually serves (singular `/message`), matching `poll.py` and `fire-probe.py`.
- An HTTP error status (404/401) or an empty/unparseable body can never be read as 'zero messages': the gate fails closed and the session is not added to recovery candidates.
- The session-exists check above it has the same fail-closed property: an error body without an `id` is not treated as 'session gone'.
- The stub in `test/test_claimant.py` pins the correct path, and a regression test feeds a 404-empty-body response and asserts no recovery candidate (and no DELETE / binding clear) results.

items.body:
## Summary

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/poll.py` reaches the laptop OpenCode server with HTTP Basic auth read from `~/.local/state/opencode/service-prod.json` (`_server_get`). `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py` reaches the **same server on the same port with plain `curl -s` and no auth at all** — every one of its six server calls (session create, per-id get, messages, delete ×3).

Verified against `http://127.0.0.1:13420` on 2026-11-08:

```
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:13420/api/session
401
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' http://127.0.0.1:13420/api/session
401
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:13420/api/session/nope
401
  body: {"_tag":"UnauthorizedError","message":"Authentication required"}
$ curl -s -m 5 -o /dev/null ...   # curl exit status
0                                 # <- 401 is still a "successful" curl
```

## Consequences in the live path

1. **Session creation cannot succeed.** `POST /api/session` returns `{"_tag":"UnauthorizedError",...}` with no `id`. `launch_step` therefore takes `session_id = None`, falls into the location check, and records the skip `session_wrong_location` — a wrong reason for a wrong cause. Live mode can never create a session, so it can never bind, so the claimant's whole live path is a no-op against this server.
2. **`returncode == 0` is not a success test for the delete.** `supervision_step` gates its delete on `delete_result.returncode == 0`. A 401 satisfies that. Today the zero-message gate happens to block it (`len(json.loads('{"_tag":...,"message":...}')) == 2`, not 0), so the recovery path does not fire — but the *only* thing preventing "clear the binding while the session still exists" (the duplicate-execution defect the delete-before-reclaim ordering exists to prevent) is an accidental len() of an error body. That is exactly the fail-open shape the packet's step 1b forbids.
3. The same applies to `GET /api/session/<id>` and `/messages`: an error body is parsed as JSON, so any code that reads `returncode` alone will treat an auth failure as a session/zero-message fact.

Note the correct credentialed path already exists in this repo: `pm-stack/dispatch/src/opencode.ts` sends the Basic header on the same v2 API.

## Suggested acceptance

1. One transport helper in `claimant.py` (Basic auth from the same auth file `poll.py` uses, honouring `OPENCODE_AUTH_FILE`), used by every server call; no bare `curl` without the header.
2. Judge every server response by **status/body shape**, never by `curl` exit status alone: a non-2xx or an `_tag` error body is an unknown/failed read, not "gone" and not "deleted".
3. Test that fails today: with the stub transport returning 401 for `POST /api/session`, assert the skip reason names auth/transport, not `session_wrong_location`; and with 401 for a session GET + messages read, assert the task is **left bound** (unknown state, fail closed) with no recovery `bind` argv emitted.
4. No credential value in logs — the helper may report *which* auth source was used, never the token.

Found by the laptop opencode-lane claimant fire 2026-11-08 (shadow), #3026 slice 1. Related: #7366 (mode not enforced), #7356 (missing launch steps), #4912 (session contract), #7085 (dispatch auth-file parsing).

## Acceptance criteria

- Every `claimant.py` call to the OpenCode server (session create, per-id get, messages, delete ×3) carries the same HTTP Basic auth `poll.py` reads from `~/.local/state/opencode/service-prod.json` — no unauthenticated `curl -s` remains in the claimant.
- A non-2xx response is never treated as success anywhere in the claimant: the delete/recovery gate checks the HTTP status (and body), not curl's exit code, so a 401 can never read as a completed step.
- A live-mode fire against the laptop server (127.0.0.1:13420) creates a session successfully (today it always 401s), and the recovery path's gates behave identically under a stubbed 401.

## Direction (Drew, 2026-10-31)

Atlas moves from a single canonical DB + one Turso publish to provenance-first, scalable infrastructure. Design doc: hatch-personal `workspace/turso-atlas/docs/atlas-provenance-and-scale-design-2026-10-31.md`.

Rules:
1. Keep ALL data — nothing stripped from atlas.db or publishes to save space; only byte-identical dupes are cleaned, backups kept.
2. Backups AND plain extracts for every corpus.
3. Every chunk records EVERY place it was found: `chunk_occurrences` (chunk → array of source locators with spans, observed_at). Today dedup silently drops occurrences (~127K at first ingest); 6,344 canonical sessions own zero chunks for exactly this reason and their occurrences are unrecorded.
4. Every import is interned content-addressed (laptop extracts CAS / R2, registry maps CA hash → normal paths) or pinned as `repo@commit:path`. Registry also holds line numbers / dates / spans for extracts.
5. Retrieval: vector/FTS search across multiple Turso shard DBs (collection × month) returns IDs; a catalog/registry resolves an ID to a file, a chunk, or a start–end section — including a member of a tar in R2 (sidecar index, range fetch) or a local file.

Verified state feeding this (2026-10-31): canonical 18,325 sessions / 122,124 messages / 107,639 chunks; local-only = 6,941 chunks of personal-client TEXT held back from Turso by policy (not missing embeddings); Turso atlas 1.0 GB / 100,698 chunks; laptop ~/atlas 12 GB contains NO consequential byte-identical duplicates (hash-verified) — it is distinct versions/working sets, so no cleanup windfall exists.

## Phases
1. Add `chunk_occurrences` + `cas_registry` to canonical atlas.db; ingest writes occurrences from now on (no re-embed, no republish).
2. Laptop extracts dir + CAS; atlas-backup covers it; backfill extracts for sources still on disk.
3. Occurrence backfill from CAS extracts; document the local-only publish predicate in the publish script.
4. Catalog DB + shard layout at next publish growth (or full message-archive ingest); resolution as MCP tools (search → ids → resolve → fetch span).

<!-- agent-note:v1 agent=muse state=filed source=main-chat-2026-10-31 -->

## Acceptance criteria

- A `chunk_occurrences` provenance registry exists: every chunk records every source locator it was found at (with spans and observed_at), including occurrences previously dropped by dedup.
- Backups AND plain extracts exist for every corpus; imports are interned content-addressed (CAS hash → path registry) or pinned as `repo@commit:path`, with line numbers / dates / spans recorded for extracts.
- Retrieval works across multiple Turso shard DBs (collection × month): vector/FTS search returns IDs and the catalog/registry resolves an ID to a file, chunk, or start–end section (including a tar member in R2 via sidecar index + range fetch, or a local file).
- No data is stripped to save space; only byte-identical duplicates are cleaned, with backups kept.

## Finding

`verify_slice1_implementation.sh` Check 2 greps `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py` for the literal constant definition `ACTIVE_WINDOW_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000`, but claimant.py no longer defines `ACTIVE_WINDOW_MS` at all — the only remaining mention is a comment (claimant.py:708) noting the constant is gone. The verifier therefore fails Check 2 on current main even though the slice-1 counting defect (#12135) is fixed.

## Evidence (current main, verified 2026-11-23 by Lane TX)

- `grep -n "ACTIVE_WINDOW" pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py` returns only line 708, a comment; no constant definition exists.
- Running the verifier (staged HOME with mode file `shadow`, so Check 1 passes): Check 1 ✓, Check 2 first sub-check (`CONCURRENCY_CAP = 36`) ✓, then `✗ ACTIVE_WINDOW_MS not found or incorrect` and the script exits 1 via `check_failed` — a genuine stale expectation, not the #12135 arithmetic defect (the script now runs and reports).

## Suggested fix shape

Update Check 2 to assert whatever replaced the active-window constant in claimant.py (or drop the sub-check if the concept was removed deliberately), and re-run the verifier to its summary so the remaining checks (3 onward) are exercised too — they have not run against current main in this pass and may carry further drift.

items.body:
## Summary

Queue task **6722** (`repo-health-code-pilot`, issue #1348) is bound to session `ses_e5e60bd3d74ffewwDg1Qd0n2Qa`, and that session is alive but has **zero messages**. No rule in the claimant contract can unstick it:

- it is not a launch candidate (it carries `progress.session_id`, and `poll.py::is_candidate` excludes bound tasks);
- the one permitted prompt resend was already spent by an earlier fire (`progress.reason: "prompt_async failed after one resend to same bound session"`, `progress.error_type: "HTTPError"`);
- the expired-lease relaunch rule in step 1 applies only when the session is **gone** — this one answers `GET /api/session/<id>` with 200.

State observed 2026-11-03T04:43Z:

| field | value |
| --- | --- |
| status | `claimed` |
| stage | `handed_off` |
| attempts | 3 / 3 |
| lease_until | 2026-11-03T04:43:41Z (expired) |
| session messages | 0 |
| session markers | no `time.idle`, no `outcome`, `created == updated` (2026-11-03T04:35:14Z) |

## Impact

The task occupies a claimed slot forever: no worker, no terminal state, and no path back to the candidate list. Its lease long-expired claim also keeps a queue row claimed, which suppresses dedupe for issue #1348.

## Proposed fix

Add a recovery rule for the "created, never prompted, never active" case, distinct from the gone-session rule. For example: a bound session with zero messages and no activity for N minutes, whose task lease has expired, may be **reclaimed to unbound** (checkpoint `stage: "launch_failed"`, clear `session_id`, keep the prior id in an audit field) so the next fire can relaunch it normally; or the task is terminally `fail`ed once `attempts >= max_attempts` is reached, with the bound session id in `--execution`. Either choice must be explicit, because "do nothing" is the current outcome.

Whichever rule wins, it should also tell Tend's fleet-watchdog (ledger backstop) what it did, since the watchdog sees the same stuck row.

## Acceptance criteria

- A bound session with zero messages, no activity markers, and an expired task lease has an explicit recovery path: either the task is reclaimed to unbound (checkpoint stage launch_failed, session_id cleared with the prior id kept in an audit field) so a later fire can relaunch it, or it is terminally failed with the bound session id recorded in the execution outcome.
- The chosen rule is written into the claimant contract/instructions, including the inactivity threshold N.
- Tend's fleet-watchdog (ledger backstop) is told what the rule did (or can read it from the task's progress), so both supervisors agree on the row's state.
- A live, progressing bound session is never reclaimed or relaunched over (existing hard rule preserved).

items.body:
## Problem

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py` — the opencode lane claimant/executor — calls two modules it never imports at module level, so in live mode its two active steps can never do their work:

- `requests` is used at lines 197, 226, 252 (`supervision_step`: session GET, messages GET, session DELETE) and 392, 407, 432 (`launch_step`: session POST, cleanup DELETEs) but is never imported (imports at lines 18–24 are only `json, os, sys, time, datetime, pathlib, typing`). `requests` is also **not installed** on the laptop (`python3 -c "import requests"` → `ModuleNotFoundError`), so a bare `import requests` would not fix the deployed environment either; the sibling `poll.py` in the same directory does its HTTP with stdlib `urllib.request`.
- `subprocess` is imported only locally inside `run_poll` (line 93) but used at module scope in `supervision_step` (line 172 list, line 259 bind) and `launch_step` (line 418 bind), where the name does not exist.

Every failure is swallowed by the broad `except Exception` handlers around these steps, so nothing crashes and nothing is logged as an error:

- Supervision: the per-queue `subprocess.run` raises `NameError`, caught by the outer handler as a generic "Supervision check failed" warning. Even with that fixed alone, the session check `requests.get` raises `NameError`, caught by the inner handler whose comment reads "Could not verify session - leave bound" — every bound session is left bound forever, and zero-message/gone-session recovery (the step's whole purpose) never fires.
- Launch: the session-create `requests.post` raises `NameError`, caught per-candidate as a `launch_error: name 'requests' is not defined` skip — and `launch_step`'s `skips` list is never returned or logged (`main()` calls `log_fire(mode, [], launched, cap_room, [])` with an empty skips list), so `fires.jsonl` records only "Launched 0" with no reason. Even past that, the bind `subprocess.run` would raise the same way.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop, main @65beb42c1a)

Probe `~/git/fleet/probe-claimant-requests` (real `claimant.py` copied verbatim; transport and queue CLI stubbed):

- `hasattr(module, "requests")` → `False`; `hasattr(module, "subprocess")` → `False`.
- `launch_step("live", 3)` with one valid unbound `handed_off` candidate from a stubbed `run_poll` → `[]` (nothing launched, no error surfaced). With stub `requests` and `subprocess` injected into the module namespace, the identical call → one launched session (`ses_1` bound).
- `supervision_step("live")` with a stubbed queue list returning a claimed opencode task whose session 404s with zero messages: with only `subprocess` stubbed (requests still missing) → `[]`; with both stubbed → the task is recovered as a `zero_message` candidate and the delete+bind recovery runs.
- First probe round (no stubs at all) printed `Supervision check failed for queue <each of the 4 queues>: name 'subprocess' is not defined` — the exact warning shape a live run would emit.
- CI never catches this: `.github/workflows/pm-stack-tests.yml` runs only `test_poll.py` for this package (per #6091/#5951); `claimant.py` has no test suite at all.

Related: #6533 (handed-off tasks are never launched — executed_lane/session_id stay null). #6533 suspects poll visibility for parked tasks; this issue is a second, independent break in the same launch path: even a candidate the poll *does* surface in `handed_off` stage cannot launch. Both need fixing for a handoff to result in a session.

## Why it matters

The claimant is the component that turns handed-off opencode-lane queue tasks into running sessions and recovers dead bound sessions. As shipped, live mode is inert: it polls, passes its own gate and cap checks, launches nothing, recovers nothing, and its fire log shows no reason — the failure mode is indistinguishable from "no work to do", which is how it can persist unnoticed alongside #6533.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `claimant.py` performs its session HTTP calls through a module that exists in the deployed environment (stdlib `urllib`, following `poll.py`'s pattern in the same directory, or a declared/installed dependency), and `subprocess` is available at module scope.
- [ ] A regression test exercises `launch_step` with a stubbed transport/queue CLI and a valid `handed_off` candidate and asserts a session is launched and bound; a second test exercises `supervision_step` recovering a gone, zero-message session. The suite is wired into `pm-stack-tests.yml` alongside `test_poll.py`.
- [ ] `launch_step`'s skips are returned and recorded in the `fires.jsonl` entry (no more hard-coded empty skips in `main()`), so a zero-launch fire states why.
- [ ] Negative control: the new tests fail against the pre-fix `claimant.py`.

items.title: opencode-claimant: binding rate - standing claimant stuck in shadow mode, cap starved launches (12 to 36)
items.body:
## Summary

The fleet queue's claimant binding rate is the OpenCode throughput bottleneck (ID program census, 2026-11-05 ~03:22 CST; Drew's directive 2026-11-05: "fix it"). Tasks claimed by Muse shift lanes and handed off to the opencode execution lane sit unbound while the laptop has session headroom. Diagnosis below was measured fresh on 2026-11-05 ~15:05-15:20Z; every consequential figure was read twice (two early reads of the claimant fire log in this session were fabricated by the tool layer and were discarded — the figures below are the grep/poll-verified ones).

## Diagnosis

1. **The standing claimant launches nothing: its mode file is `shadow`.** `~/.local/state/opencode-claimant/mode` = `shadow` (verified 3x). The OpenChamber claimant task fires every 10 min and, per prompt.md, shadow mode discovers and reports but never claims/binds/launches — a slice-1 safety gate left pending a "parallel-run gate" packet that never landed. Its 2026-11-05T15:10:00Z fire saw 43 candidates, computed cap_room 2, launched 0.
2. **All actual binding is ad-hoc.** `~/.local/state/opencode-claimant/inflight.jsonl` (grep-verified: 108 lines, 29 `bound` events) shows every bind since 2026-11-04T14:23Z came from agent-driven `drive_fire.py` batches (max 6 per drive, hardcoded order) — i.e. an operator session happening to drive it. Last bind 2026-11-05T09:13:45Z; **zero binds in the ~6h before this fix** while 26-43 candidates waited. The census's "2 claimant sessions launching serially" were these manual drives.
3. **The cap starves launches even when live.** CAP = 12 active root sessions server-wide (poll.py, claimant.py, prompt.md), counted across ALL server tenants — scheduled lane runners, the claimant's own session, zombies (see the filed note `issue-5016-cap-composition` in the claimant state dir: cap_room 0 with 44 candidates on 2026-11-03). Live read at fix time: 10 active roots -> cap_room 2. The census ran 18-19 roots at load 4.5-7.5 on 16 cores, so 12 is below demonstrated headroom.
4. **Per-launch cost is not the problem.** Driven batches bind at ~2-4 s/task (inflight timestamps). Serialization that matters = shadow mode (0 launches) + 10-min fire cadence executed by an LLM session working prompt.md step-by-step + cap_room ~0-2.
5. **The deterministic executor was never committed.** `claimant.py` (the prompt.md implementation: supervision, gate, cap, launch loop, fire log) exists only as an untracked file in the laptop primary checkout. The repo ships poll.py/prompt.md/install.mjs but not the executor, so the fleet kept running the LLM-prompt form.
6. **Watchdog reconciliation — same root.** `agent.claim_repo_task` (migration-0023) only returns tasks with `attempts < max_attempts` and `not_before` due. A handed-off task whose lease expires unbound returns to `queued` with attempts+1; re-claim + re-handoff loops burn attempts until the task is permanently unclaimable while still counted in `queued_count`. That is why worker-shift lanes sporadically report all-null claims against a deep queue (and their watchdog failure streaks: repo-queue-worker-shift-nix cf=6, -openchamber cf=25, -opencode cf=24, -openchamber-b cf=14 at the 06:10 check): claim-side eligibility divergence, produced by the bind-side failure. Health attempts distribution shows the pile-up (135 tasks at exactly 24 attempts).

## Before-metrics (2026-11-05 ~15:05-15:15Z, two reads)

- repo-health-code-pilot: queued 205 -> 202, claimed 31 -> 36, parked 247 -> 243, blocked 215
- Unbound claimant candidates (poll.py): 26 (code 18, openchamber 4, nix 3, opencode 1)
- Active root sessions 10 / cap 12 -> cap_room 2
- Binds in the last ~25h: 29, all ad-hoc; binds in the last 6h: 0
- Candidate claim leases: 45 min; sampled candidates had already waited >= 40 min unbound

## Fix (this issue's PR)

- Commit `claimant.py` (pre-existing untracked implementation) so the deterministic executor is versioned.
- CAP 12 -> 20 in poll.py, claimant.py, prompt.md (headroom-matched; active-root counting with the 30-min window unchanged; fires still launch at most cap_room).
- claimant.py: single-instance flock (overlapping fires can never double-launch) + bounded parallel launch pool (4 workers) across distinct candidates; exactly-once stays anchored on the atomic DB bind (`bind_repo_task_lane_session`), with re-verification inside each worker and session cleanup on bind failure (existing behavior).
- Claimant task cadence */10 -> */5 (install.mjs CRON) and the task prompt directs the fire to execute claimant.py deterministically.
- Runtime: reinstall the task (enabled) and flip the mode file to `live`.

## Follow-ups named, not fixed here

- Attempts-capped queued tasks (the 24-attempt pile-up) are unclaimable until their attempts/max_attempts are revisited — a separate queue-data decision.
- Cap composition visibility: the fire log reports totals only; per-tenant composition (lane runners vs bound workers vs other) would make future cap tuning direct (partially covered by the issue-5016 note).

items.body:
## Summary

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py` (HEAD `9f5a92057d`, restored by #7290) has the correct create → verify-location → bind ordering, but **stops after bind**. Step 4d builds the worker prompt as a string and never delivers it:

```python
# claimant.py:474-489
# Step 4d: Send prompt to bound session
prompt = f"""
Execute queue task {task_id}
...
"""
# In a real implementation, this would send the prompt via the session API
# For now, we just record the successful launch
launched.append({"task_id": task_id, "session_id": session_id, ...})
```

There is no `POST` to `/api/session/<id>` (or any message endpoint) anywhere in `launch_step`. A live fire therefore **creates and binds a session that never receives a prompt**.

## Why this is urgent now

Two things changed today:

1. #7290 merged (#6865 closed 06:31:52Z), so `claimant.py` again has working supervision and a live launch path.
2. #7325 is the only remaining gate: `poll.py` cannot read the queues. Once that lands, live mode stops being a no-op and starts doing this on every launch.

A bound-but-never-prompted session is exactly the state #4758's recovery rule exists to clean up. So every launch would produce one zero-message session that supervision then has to delete and reclaim 30+ minutes later — a self-inflicted oscillating loop rather than forward progress.

## Also missing from the spec'd launch sequence (all zero-hit `grep`s in `claimant.py`)

| Spec step | Required | At HEAD |
|---|---|---|
| 4c | `checkpoint <id> --worker <worker_id> --stage launched` with session id in progress | absent |
| 4d | send the queue runbook prompt to the bound session, `--worker <worker_id>` on every verb, terminal `--execution {"lane":"opencode","session_id":"<id>"}` | **string built, never sent** |
| 4e | agent-note `agent-note:v1`, state=handed off, task id + session id | absent |
| gate | skip candidates whose issue carries `held` / `user/owned` / `do-not-merge` / `do-not-auto-edit` | absent (no label read at all) |
| gate | `attempts < max_attempts` before relaunch | absent |
| §EXECUTION | single-instance lock + bounded parallel pool | absent |

On the last row: the task prompt's EXECUTION section states `claimant.py` "launches distinct candidates in parallel under a bounded pool and a single-instance lock". Neither exists — the loop is serial with no `flock`/`O_EXCL`/`ThreadPool`. Fire cadence is 10 min and a fire can take minutes, so two overlapping fires are possible and would both walk the same candidate list; the atomic bind is what keeps exactly-once, but the lock the description relies on is not there.

## What does work

- Session create body uses the correct v2 shape (`location: {directory}`, `model: {id, providerID}`, `agent`).
- `location.directory` is verified against `PRIMARY_CLONE` before bind, with delete-on-mismatch.
- Bind happens before anything that can interleave, and a bind failure deletes the created session.
- Supervision has the zero-message delete-before-reclaim ordering.

## Suggested acceptance

1. `launch_step` `POST`s the prompt to the bound session id before recording the candidate as launched; on send failure, reconcile (read the session's messages) rather than relaunch, per the task's step 5.
2. Add `checkpoint --stage launched` and the 4e agent-note.
3. Read the issue labels and skip on any of the four hard-stop labels; skip when `attempts >= max_attempts`.
4. Add the single-instance lock and the bounded pool, or drop the claim from the task description.
5. Test that fails today: with a stub session create + bind, assert a prompt `POST` to `/api/session/ses_new1` occurs, and that a send error produces a reconciled skip rather than a second launch.

Found by the laptop opencode-lane claimant fire 2026-11-08 (shadow). Related: #7325, #6865, #4758, #4912, #5400.

## Acceptance criteria

- A live launch delivers the worker prompt to the bound session via the session API (a POST to the session's message endpoint) before the launch is recorded as successful — create → verify-location → bind → send-prompt, in that order.
- A bound session after a live fire has exactly the intended first message (verifiable via the server), never zero messages.
- If the prompt send fails, the launch is recorded as failed (and the binding is not left masquerading as a working lane).

Design (fleet design architect, pass 44): **the claimant judges and drives sessions per-id under the v2 contract, and every bound state has a named next step.** Full design doc: `files/designs/code-claimant-session-contract.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace.

## Problem

The opencode-claimant (`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/` — `poll.py` + `prompt.md`, #3026 slice 1) talks to the OpenCode v2 server through three seams whose contract was never stated, and each has now filed:

1. **Judging from a list page** — #4757: `poll.py` treats one `GET /api/session` read as the complete list; it truncates at 50, so cap accounting overstates `cap_room` (launching past the 12 cap becomes possible) and supervision reads live bound sessions as gone — against the claimant's own "never relaunch over a live session" rule.
2. **Creating under the wrong contract** — #4870: `prompt.md` step 4b's create body sends a top-level `directory`, which v2 strips; launched workers land in `/home/user`, not the repo primary. The dispatch client already sends the correct shape (`location: { directory }`, `pm-stack/dispatch/src/opencode.ts:52-58`).
3. **A bound state with no next step** — #4758: a bound session that is alive with zero messages (task 6722, resend already spent, lease expired) is reachable by no rule: not a candidate (bound), not gone (answers per-id), resend exhausted. Claimed forever.

## Recorded decisions

1. **Per-id judging.** Cap counts from the `/api/session/active` id set directly (per-id GET for root-ness); supervision existence/progress is a per-id read in `poll.py` and in `prompt.md` steps 1 + 5. Any list read that remains fails closed (`cap_room: null`) when the returned count equals the page size — the same treatment `summarize_cap` already gives an unreadable active set.
2. **Verify before bind.** Step 4b's body becomes the v2 shape (`location: {directory}`), and the create response's `location.directory` must equal the requested repo primary **before** binding; a mismatch is a creation failure (task stays unbound, failure checkpointed) and the misplaced session is deleted per-id. Mechanical, because two text-only shape fixes in this prompt (`model` object, task 5857; now `directory`) have each cost a launch window.
3. **Every bound state has one disposition** (table in the design doc). For the never-prompted state (zero messages, no markers, 30 min inactive — reusing `poll.py`'s `ACTIVE_WINDOW_MS` — lease expired): **reclaim to unbound while attempts remain** (DELETE the verified-empty session first — delete failure keeps the binding; checkpoint `launch_failed`, prior session id kept in an audit field), and **terminally fail at `attempts >= max_attempts`** with the session id in `--execution` (task 6722's case). The outcome lands on the task's progress, which is what Tend's fleet-watchdog reads — agreement via the shared record, no new channel.

Alternatives and why they lose (paginate-the-list; text-only create fix; fail-only recovery; reclaim without delete) are recorded in the design doc, as are the open questions (queue-read page-size rule — no evidence; active-set read bound — no evidence).

## Phases (adopted origins — do not re-file or split)

- **Phase 1 = #4757** — per-id judging: cap + supervision.
- **Phase 2 = #4870** — v2 create shape + verify-before-bind (independent).
- **Phase 3 = #4758** — never-prompted recovery as decided above (independent).
- **Phase 4 = closing audit (new, filed with this design)** — server-call inventory against the contract, state table into the claimant README, origin closure; gated on Phases 1–3.

Originated on the trigger recorded at design pass 42 (a third claimant-contract filing); #4757/#4758 re-verified this pass as still `status/needs-triage`, unsplit, unclaimed.

The fleet monitor's run-start digest (`monitor-digest.py`, used by repo-fleet-monitor per code#2154) flags 134 developing-today/code issues under `queue_queued_missing_task` — issues labelled `queue/queued` that the digest believes have no live queue task. ## Evidence
- Fleet monitor run 2026-11-08 18:12 CST (run_id f52bdf5a-f312-4fe7-87fe-479ecf51b784): "Digest defect: queue_queued_missing_task over-flags 134 code items; sample of 3 all had live tasks via dedupe hit, indicating unhealthy join logic."

items.body:
## Problem

In `pkgs/chat` (`main.go`, main `4b0f9ceb`), every client's model keeps its entire chat history forever and rebuilds the whole viewport content on every message:

```go
case chatMsg:
    m.messages = append(m.messages, m.senderStyle.Render(msg.id)+": "+msg.text)
    m.viewport.SetContent(strings.Join(m.messages, "\n"))
    m.viewport.GotoBottom()
```

(`main.go:177-180`; the field is declared at `:113` and initialised at `:144`.)

Those are the only three references to `messages` in the file: nothing ever caps, trims, or windows the slice. The viewport is 5 lines tall (`viewport.New(30, 5)`, `:141-143`), so nearly everything retained is invisible — yet a long-lived session's model grows without bound, and each new message costs a `strings.Join` over the full history: total rendering work is quadratic in the number of messages the session has seen, and the joined string is re-allocated whole every time.

This is the per-session sibling of #3201 (the server-side `progs` registry in the same file, which is never pruned either): #3201 covers the server retaining dead programs; this issue covers a single live session's own history and render cost, which grows even while the session is healthy and connected.

## Evidence (verified this run)

- Code: `grep -n messages pkgs/chat/main.go` returns exactly three sites — field `:113`, init `:144`, append+Join `:178-179`. No cap, trim, or ring buffer anywhere in the package (the package is the single `main.go`, 197 lines).
- Laptop probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-laneB-chathistory/`, plain Go replicating the append + full `strings.Join` performed per `chatMsg`; `pkgs/chat/main.go` sha256 `70e8215c5d13db1fb…` identical on the sandbox clone at `4b0f9ceb` and the laptop clone `~/git/code`):

```text
n= 1000  total append+Join time=8ms     retained messages=1000
n= 5000  total append+Join time=135ms   retained messages=5000
n=10000  total append+Join time=480ms   retained messages=10000
n=20000  total append+Join time=1.898s  retained messages=20000
```

Doubling the history roughly quadruples the total work — the per-message Join dominates, exactly as the code shape predicts.

Dedup: open + closed search for chat message history / viewport returns only #3201 (server `progs` registry: fan-out to dead programs + data race). No existing issue covers the per-model `messages` slice.

## Why it matters

The chat server is a long-running SSH service: a busy room or a client left connected for days steadily eats more memory per session and gets visibly laggier with every message, because each keystroke-era message re-renders history the 5-line viewport will never show. It degrades exactly in the long-lived-session case the service exists for, and there is no operator-visible bound to tune.

## Acceptance criteria

- A session's retained history is bounded by a named cap (sized relative to what the viewport can show / scroll back, and documented in the code), or the viewport content is built incrementally without re-joining the full history per message.
- After the cap is reached, older messages are dropped from the model (the visible behaviour — latest messages shown, `GotoBottom` — is unchanged).
- Per-message render work no longer grows with total history length once the cap is reached.
- A test or benchmark pins the behaviour: feeding more messages than the cap leaves the retained count at the cap and the newest message visible.

items.body:
## Problem

`app.send` in `pkgs/chat/main.go` fans a chat message out with one new goroutine per recipient (`go p.Send(msg)`, main.go:52-54). Nothing serializes those goroutines, so:

1. **Broadcast order is not preserved.** Two messages sent in order can be delivered to a session in the opposite order whenever the first `Send` is delayed (a busy program, scheduler timing). Different sessions can therefore show the same conversation in different orders, and one session can show a reply before the message it answers.
2. **A stalled session accumulates unbounded goroutines.** `tea.Program.Send` blocks until the program's update loop reads the message (or the program ends). A session that stops reading — a wedged terminal, a dead-but-not-yet-pruned connection — leaves one blocked goroutine per broadcast message, forever, with no bound, coalescing, or drop.

## Evidence (main @ 30ce6be56, verified this run)

- `pkgs/chat/main.go:46-55` — `send` copies the registry under `RLock`, then `for _, p := range progs { go p.Send(msg) }`. The `go` is presumably there because `send` is called from inside a model's `Update` (main.go:205-211) and the sender's own program is in the registry, so a naive synchronous `Send` to itself could block its own update loop — but the goroutine-per-recipient shape trades that for ordering and pile-up.
- Laptop probe (verbatim `main.go`/`main_test.go` from current main, md5 main.go ed60f0ca59fe0cec95101087ca792655; probe dir `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-02-laneB-chatorder/` on the laptop):
  - PROBE1: a recipient whose `Send` for the text `first` sleeps 150 ms before recording received two broadcasts issued in order `[first second]` as `[second first]` — order inverted at one recipient.
  - PROBE2: 40 broadcasts to one recipient whose `Send` never returns grew the goroutine count by exactly 40 — one permanently blocked goroutine per message, unbounded.
  - The existing registry tests (`TestSendReachesOnlyLivePrograms`, `TestRemoveUnknownIsNoOp`, `TestRegistryConcurrentRegisterSendRemove`) all pass alongside the probes.

## Why it matters

A chat room's one shared truth is the order of its messages. Today that order is per-session luck: two participants can read the same exchange in opposite orders with no error anywhere. And the pile-up half turns one stalled SSH session into slow, unbounded goroutine growth on the server for as long as the room stays busy — the registry pruning from #3201 only helps once the program actually ends, not while it is wedged.

## Acceptance criteria

- Broadcasts are delivered to each live program in the order `send` was called: a probe in the style of PROBE1 (a recipient whose first `Send` is delayed) records `[first second]`, and a multi-recipient probe shows every recipient recording the same order.
- A recipient that never reads cannot accumulate goroutines without bound: the fan-out drops, coalesces, or queues with a stated bound for a stalled program (PROBE2-style measurement stays bounded as broadcasts continue), and the session is still pruned normally when its program ends.
- Sending a message from a session still delivers it to that same session (no self-send deadlock): the sender sees its own message exactly once, in order.
- Existing `pkgs/chat` tests pass; new tests pin both the ordering and the bounded-stalled-recipient behaviour using the existing `sender` interface / `fakeProg` harness.

Distinct from #3201 (closed: registry never pruned — this is the fan-out call shape that fix kept, not the registry lifecycle) and from #3209 (graceful shutdown exits 1, the `Start`/`ListenAndServe` path, unrelated to `send`).

# Fleet CA, credentials & secrets — v0.3 design mill (Summit build-out)

**Program epic.** Design-mill run ordered by Drew 2026-11-12 19:28 CST: run the Fleet v0.3 credentials/secrets/CA package through the design mill — preserve every requirement, break it into reviewed component designs, and turn each design into linked, testable implementation issues. A completed design is NOT a completed implementation epic; implementation children stay open until their own acceptance gates pass.

**Intrinsic urgency: 450 (High)** — ahead of normal actionable work (PM charter bands). Dispatch directive: direct Summit session, launched and verified by the orchestrator (this issue's comments carry the launch receipt).

## Authoritative sources (read as ONE intake; precedence: Drew's current instructions → dated addendum refinements → v0.3 spec baseline → decision review proposals → historical inputs)

1. **Muse handoff — Fleet CA, Credentials & Secrets** (Google Doc, modified 2026-11-12): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1yeSWQvMIer92zQ4lj99TsTH2oXZem0WfH-WMYKYJpJ0

All sources are merged into the repo design directory (see the docs PR linked in comments) and staged on the laptop at `~/.local/share/fleet/intake/fleet-ca-v03-20261112/` (zip hash re-verified after transfer). Repo pinned at intake: `6a7843cae59878e10071f27440b93489053dbc68` (2026-11-12).

## Binding constraints (Drew)

- **ML-DSA-44 is the baseline signature scheme** for the CA design.
- **The Merkle-tree experiment (Cloudflare MTC) is OPTIONAL** — a separate, non-blocking controlled-stack research track; never a v1 dependency. (Handoff doc carries the full MTC analysis: inclusion proofs vs whole certs, landmark/cosigner provisioning, PQ-only separation, byte/CPU/latency comparison against the shortest conventional ML-DSA chain.)

## Scope (from the handoff doc — the CA/credentials workstream, NOT the PM-stack redesign)

Unified secret records + BWS/op/bw adapters (three DIFFERENT provider products — never conflated); daily three-way reconciliation with recoverable `zz.delete` history and false-delete prevention; audit/event journal + provider performance benchmarks; fnox library evaluation (near-term priority); SOPS/age/NixOS integration; password, SSH and iroh generation; reusable Rust APIs + the existing Fleet multicall CLI (no competing tool); PKI root/issuer/leaf lifecycle, publication, packaging, client trust and verification; nonblocking OpenBao/federation/infrastructure research.

**Reference PKI (spec controls):** four independent roots (Ed25519, P-256, RSA, ML-DSA-44), nine asymmetric root cross-certificates (ML-DSA root never signs classical roots by default), Base + Internal Web issuer sets with independent A/B partitions and eligible direct issuer cross-signatures — **20 CA key pairs / 65 CA certificate variants before leaves**. Reference expiries: roots `2050-07-07T12:00:00Z`, both issuer sets `2032-07-07T12:00:00Z` (distinct from the normal 20y/5y/90d defaults). RSA-2048 is a policy-gated compatibility option, not the default long-lived root. Root signing always requires an explicitly authorized signer source — never silently discover/exercise root keys.

**Root custody (addendum refinement):** initial roots escrowed to exactly three approved destinations — encrypted laptop storage, the authorized BWS project, the authorized 1Password vault — with integrity checks and tested restoration; NOT auto-extended to every future provider. R2 is a researched additional destination, not automatic authorization. Offline/hardware root signing is the future path; three OpenBao containers on one host are a lab, not three failure domains.

## V1 — what exists today (intake census; the Summit verifies and deepens)

## Safety gates (hard)

Design and synthetic proof only in this program phase. **No production CA generation or signing, no root escrow/export, no live vault writes or reconciliation, no credential rotation, no DNS/trust changes, no live service deployment** is authorized by this handoff. Domain starter issues are native sub-issues of this epic; the Summit files the granular children under them.

Orchestrator check-ins on the bound Summit session (status, questions, artifacts vs the statement inventory); stall = one nudge, then replacement, recorded here. Durable monitor: the fleet's session-minder coverage plus the supervision record in this issue's comments.

Refs #13778 — the P-384 root-identity dated design-record PR is open (branch certprog/p384-adr, head da81369e67c005fc4ff1e6922470e9466b98a1f8; two files: the new record folder plus one doc/README.md index line).
